disclosures.name: TestVersion6
disclosures.reason: runtime-capability: the upstream test is timing-sensitive by design. In google/uuid v1.6.0, NewV6 writes the version nibble over bits 12-15 of the timestamp and Time() reads those bits back, so the test reads t1 > t2 ("time reversed") whenever the clock crosses a multiple of 409.6 microseconds between its two NewV6 calls. Measured on a linux/amd64 cloud host on 2026-10-26, in fresh full-suite processes: the converted test fails 40 of 150 with tiered compilation off (the -tests host's setting) and about 64 of 150 with .NET's default tiering (65, 64 and 63 in three runs); Go fails 0 of 300; Go running the test alone in a fresh process fails 262 of 1000. The converted clock is DateTime.UtcNow, at 100 ns resolution, so resolution is not the cause. The cause of the wider gap between the converted side's two calls is undetermined: turning tiering off lowers the rate rather than removing it. A run in which the converted test passes reports this entry as orphaned and reads 54 + 0; a run in which it fails reads 53 + 1. The proof is the count one unretried run reads, either way.
